question.value: What are the internal structure and dynamics of the CMZ cloud G0.253+0.016, and is it a single coherent centrally-condensed cloud or a hierarchically structured complex of line-of-sight components?

evidence.quote: In this paper we provide a comprehensive description of the internal dynamics of G0.253+0.016 (a.k.a. ‘the Brick’)
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00217.S.
This paper makes use of the ALMA Early Science Cycle 0 Band 3 observations of G0.253+0.016 originally presented in (cite: rathborne_2014; rathborne_2015).

we select the HNCO 4(0,4)–3(0,3) transition (rest freq. $\approx~87.925$ GHz) as our primary tracer of the kinematics since it is bright and extended.

analysis_steps.goal: Decompose HNCO spectra into Gaussian components

method.value: scousepy semi-automated multi-component Gaussian fitting with spectral averaging areas, manual fits in pyspeckit, then automated fitting of all pixels

evidence.quote: The spatially averaged spectra extracted from each SAA are then manually fitted by the user. Fitting is performed interactively using pyspeckit

key_parameters.value: T1=3.0, T2=1.0, T3=T4=3.0, T5=0.5; spectra with peak below 0.03 mJy/beam masked

evidence.quote: We set both of these tolerance levels to 3.0.

assumptions.value: spectra decomposable into Gaussians; HNCO likely optically thin

evidence.quote: we assume that the spectra can be decomposed into individual Gaussians.

fitting.value: Best solution per pixel chosen by smallest corrected AIC

evidence.quote: the final best-fitting solution for each pixel is that which has the smallest value of the (corrected) Akaike Information Criterion

findings_qualitative.value: HNCO is likely optically thin and the cloud is a hierarchically structured complex of line-of-sight velocity components, not a single centrally condensed cloud

evidence.quote: G0.253+0.016 is a complex, hierarchically-structured molecular cloud exhibiting an intricate network of velocity components situated along the line-of-sight.

claims.hypothesis: Moment analysis adequately describes the kinematics of the Brick
claims.experiment: Compare scousepy decomposition with moment maps
claims.result: Dispersion from moments is 11.1 km/s versus 4.4 km/s from fits; multiple components in ~96% of the map
claims.finding: Moment analysis misses substantial kinematic structure

evidence.quote: The mean velocity dispersion is more than a factor of 2 greater than that extracted using scousepy  which is due to the presence of multiple velocity components in the data.

claims.hypothesis: Velocity dispersions follow steep CMZ dispersion-size relations
claims.experiment: Compare measured 0.07 pc dispersions to predictions
claims.finding: Dispersions broader than predicted; possibly large line-of-sight depth

evidence.quote: These are factors of $\sim9$ and $\sim4$ narrower than those measured from our scousepy decomposition, respectively.

claims.hypothesis: The Brick is a single coherent centrally-condensed cloud with depletion
claims.experiment: Radiative transfer for HNCO optical depth and kinematic argument
claims.result: HNCO optically thin unless abundance enhanced by 1-2 orders of magnitude; PPV profile requires unobserved gradients

evidence.quote: We disfavour the interpretation that G0.253+0.016 is a centrally-condensed molecular cloud with depletion in its cold interior

claims.hypothesis: The C-shaped arc is relic evidence of formation by cloud-cloud collision
claims.experiment: acorns tree association of the arc
claims.result: Arc is ~17% of fitted components, exclusive to tree B
claims.finding: Unlikely a relic of formation of the whole cloud

evidence.quote: we dispute that the presence of the arc is residual evidence of the formation process of the cloud as a whole
